acceptance_criteria: critical threats map to preventative, detective, and recovery controls with owners and tests
privileged access is phishing-resistant-MFA bound, time-limited, independently approved, and audited
service identities are short-lived, audience/scope bound, revocable, and denied outside policy
key access, rewrap, recovery quorum, emergency revocation, and cryptographic-erasure evidence are governed
privacy inventory, impact review, subject access, rights workflows, and incident impact are durable and policy scoped
audit chains detect gaps, mutation, invalid signatures, and missing referenced manifests
external provider changes, exceptions, incidents, local-only denial, output quarantine, and privacy-safe telemetry fail closed
release promotion consumes one signed cross-component release record and remains fail-closed without required evidence
complete clean-source acceptance and independent inner/outer verification return zero findings

deferred_requirements.defer_reason: Requires signed/scanned container and Apple build artifacts plus patch-SLA evidence unavailable in this environment.
deferred_requirements.requirement: Containers and mobile builds shall be hardened, signed, scanned, and patched under defined SLAs.

deferred_requirements.defer_reason: Contractual vendor terms require external legal/procurement review; code will retain provider-purpose controls but cannot establish executed agreements.
deferred_requirements.requirement: Vendor agreements and settings shall prohibit training/use beyond approved purpose where required.

deferred_requirements.defer_reason: Legal/evidentiary admissibility requires jurisdiction-specific counsel and procedure outside software verification.
deferred_requirements.requirement: Legal/evidentiary claims shall require separate counsel and jurisdictional procedure.

dependency_rationale: OPS-001 is the first dependency-valid Phase 7 epic. OPS-003 depends on OPS-001; OPS-004 depends on OPS-003; QA-002 depends on OPS-004 and QA-001.
external_gaps: container and Apple artifact signing/scanning/patch-SLA evidence
executed vendor agreements and external privacy/legal review
frozen Node production build, Apple/LiDAR, approved LingBot/GPU, executable cloud infrastructure, penetration/accessibility/usability/legal review

included_requirements.requirement: The threat model shall enumerate capture-device compromise, upload tampering, archive bombs, parser exploits, GPU escape, cross-tenant access, signed-URL leakage, viewer scraping, model exfiltration, prompt injection, insider abuse, and destructive deletion.
Each critical threat shall map to preventative, detective, and recovery controls plus tests and owners.
Sensitive facility and family data shall use misuse/abuse cases beyond ordinary confidentiality.
The threat model shall be reviewed when adding a sensor, model provider, sharing mode, plugin, or new data purpose.
Residual risks shall be visible to release decision makers.
A public viewer shall be analyzed as hostile client code with no trusted secrets.
Threat modeling shall cover geometry/splat payload parsing, provider egress, topology disclosure, derivative redaction, authority spoofing, and immersive collision/navigation failure.
Untrusted provider outputs shall remain quarantined with malware/resource/format/transform/content validation.
Authorization shall apply to geometry derivatives even when texture or obvious personal data has been removed.
Abuse tests shall attempt to elevate proxy/design assets to verified/observed authority through API, import, UI, and export paths.
Client and CDN caches shall purge or invalidate superseded/redacted hybrid assets according to policy.
Immersive safety failures shall disable affected locomotion modes while preserving a safe fallback.
Human privileged access shall require phishing-resistant MFA where available and just-in-time elevation.
Service-to-service authentication shall use short-lived workload identities with audience and scope.
Network policies shall restrict worker egress and prevent runtime model downloads in production.
Secrets shall live in an approved secret manager and never in repositories, images, logs, manifests, or mobile packages.
Sensitive-access and administrative events shall be immutable and monitored.
All network connections shall use current approved TLS with certificate validation; local transfer uses authenticated encrypted channels.
Data keys shall be generated securely, wrapped by managed or local key-encryption keys, and scoped by policy.
Key access shall be logged with actor/workload, purpose, resource scope, and outcome.
Rotation shall support rewrapping and emergency revocation with bounded impact.
Recovery mechanisms shall avoid one-person permanent loss while respecting local-only and family succession policy.
Cryptographic erasure shall include key deletion evidence and residual replica/backup timelines.
The platform shall maintain a data inventory linking category, purpose, legal/consent basis, processors, residency, retention, security, and rights workflow.
New data purposes or providers shall require privacy impact review before processing.
Subject-access export shall explain source records, derivatives, sharing, consent, and automated processing in understandable form.
Correction/restriction/deletion requests shall be tracked and verified across canonical and derived stores.
Incident workflows shall identify affected people/projects and applicable notification decision without exposing additional data.
Audit events shall include actor/workload, action, resource, tenant/project, time, source IP/device context when appropriate, purpose, outcome, trace, and before/after references.
Capture finalization shall record package root hash, device/app, signer, and verification result.
Evidence access, model execution, authority changes, consent changes, exports, and deletion shall be audited.
Audit storage shall prevent ordinary application roles from altering or deleting events.
Verification tools shall detect gaps, broken chains, invalid signatures, and missing referenced manifests.
CI shall run formatting, type checks, unit/integration tests, schema compatibility, license/SBOM, secret scan, vulnerability scan, and artifact signing.
Mobile, web, service, worker, infrastructure, and model manifests shall share a release record.
Production deployment shall verify signatures and environment policy.
Release promotion shall require benchmark and acceptance evidence from `955_release_gates.md`.
Emergency patches shall still produce traceable artifacts and retrospective review.
Rollback shall include service, worker routing/model, configuration, and database compatibility plans.
An external or unknown provider shall not access source or derived scene bytes before an approved provider dossier and matching data/purpose policy exist.
Unknown data processing, retention, training, region, license, or security facts shall default to no production data access.
Data classification shall account for geometry, layout, inference, relationships, and security context even when textures or obvious identifiers are removed.
Manual external use shall follow controlled minimization, export, custody, receipt, import validation, independent review, and deletion/cleanup recording.

Private residential, restricted building-system, critical-infrastructure, biometric, intimate, and LiveForever-sensitive data shall be blocked from public hosted providers unless a specific higher-order approval permits it.
Provider approval shall separately cover source code, weights, datasets, dependencies, commercial rights, deployment mode, and execution artifact hashes.
Provider credentials and object access shall be short-lived, least-privilege, operation-scoped, and revoked at completion or incident.
A consented preservation or construction purpose shall not be expanded to provider training, public demonstration, or unrelated retention without separate authorization.
Approved external execution shall use destination controls, egress monitoring, content hashes, signed receipts, quarantine, and return validation appropriate to the data class.
A provider version or material terms/control change shall enter review or shadow state and shall not inherit approval automatically.
Provider exceptions shall be scoped, approved, audited, automatically expiring, and unable to waive truth, consent, legal-hold, or authority rules.
Incidents shall identify and withdraw affected source, derivative, publication, cache, and export assets while preserving investigation evidence.
Local-only deployments shall deny network-required providers by default and expose the attempted egress in audit.
SplatEdit shall remain limited to synthetic, public, or explicitly public-cleared fixtures until its production-relevant processing and permission posture is approved.
Output from an external provider shall be treated as untrusted content and parsed, scanned, registered, and validated in isolation.
Operational telemetry about provider use shall not contain raw geometry, media, transcripts, secrets, or unnecessary precise locations.
Tests shall attempt unauthorized discovery through IDs, counts, search snippets, vectors, thumbnails, tiles, caches, logs, share links, signed URLs, exports, and agent tools.
Consent restriction/revocation shall propagate to processing, viewer, search, agents, reports, notifications, exports, and future model training.
File ingestion shall test malicious archives, media parsers, oversized dimensions, embedded scripts, and metadata injection.
Agent tests shall cover destructive requests, role confusion, evidence fabrication, source-label removal, and speaking as an unconsented person.
Deletion tests shall verify canonical, derivatives, indexes, caches, links, and backup expiry behavior.
Incident and support access controls shall be exercised through realistic scenarios.

milestone: Progress 07 — OPS-001 security, privacy, audit, key-management, and supply-chain readiness
scope_statement: Bounded implementation of OPS-001 security, privacy, audit, key-management, provider-governance, and supply-chain readiness controls descending from accepted Progress 06-R2. External legal, signing/scanning, jurisdiction-specific evidence, deployment, and production controls remain deferred or externally validated.
